changes.after: Choose one path with a true-or-false check.

before: An if expression chooses which block runs. Its condition must produce true or false.
>= means greater than or equal to. For example 6 >= 6 is true; 4 >= 5 is false.
The block immediately after if runs when the condition is true. The else block runs when it is false; not both.
The condition is checked using the current value when execution reaches if.
Expected result: Ready. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: `if` chooses which block of instructions runs. Its condition is a question with a true-or-false answer.
`score >= 5` asks whether score is at least 5. An equal value counts as true.
When the condition is true, the if block runs. When it is false, the else block runs. Only one of the two messages is shown.
Rust reads score's current value when it reaches the if instruction.
The screen shows `Ready` because 7 is at least 5.
